mainTopic: יבום for a סוטה and for a man's remarried divorcée: the meaning of 'after she was defiled', and whether her צרה is also exempt.
overview: This amud deals with יבום for women who are forbidden to their husbands. It opens by defending רב: his rule that a סוטה has no יבום bond covers only a definite סוטה, while the source brought against him is about an uncertain one. The גמרא tests this with a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי בן כיפר and the חכמים argue over the פסוק 'after she was defiled'. The חכמים use it for a סוטה and a לאו, while רבי יוסי בן כיפר applies it to a man who takes back his divorcée after she married someone else. רב יהודה then asks רב ששת whether the צרה of such a remarried divorcée is free from יבום. The גמרא works out where this question really belongs, according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר or the רבנן, in two versions. Two ברייתות are brought as proof, and each proof is pushed off. In the first, the 'fit' and 'disqualified' widows can be explained through רב יוסף's lesson not to waste what others need. In the second, the wording has to be fixed anyway, and it can be fixed in a way that lets the צרה do יבום. The amud ends with רבי יוחנן's question in two versions. In one, it is whether a קל וחומר can push off the צרה. In the other, it is whether a קל וחומר can forbid the woman herself despite the מצוה of יבום.

steps.title: End of the challenge against רב: she does חליצה, not יבום
steps.stepSummary: The cited source ends by ruling that the woman 'does not do יבום', which implies she still needs חליצה. That is a challenge to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and she does not do יבום (she does חליצה instead).
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish the source the גמרא brought against רב. A woman who secluded herself after a warning, and whose husband died before she drank, does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she needs חליצה, then she does have a bond (זיקה) to the brother-in-law. That clashes with רב's view that a סוטה has no יבום bond at all.

keyTerms.meaning: She is married through יבום to her late husband's brother
The ceremony that releases a widow from the יבם
The bond between a childless widow and her late husband's brother

steps.confusionAlert: The text here starts in the middle of a quote. The words 'and she does not do יבום' are the end of the source that was brought against רב on the previous lines.

phrases.english: and she does not do levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the source quoted against רב just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a סוטה has no יבום bond
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring חליצה shows there is a bond, so a סוטה does seem to have זיקה.

steps.title: רב was talking about a definite סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רב can answer that his rule covers only a woman who was certainly unfaithful. The source is about a woman whose guilt is uncertain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could tell you: I was speaking about a definite סוטה, and you are bringing me a case of an uncertain סוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by narrowing his rule to a woman who definitely sinned. The source is about a woman who only secluded herself, so nobody knows whether she sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An uncertain סוטה might be innocent, so the bond to the יבם may still exist and she needs חליצה. A definite סוטה is forbidden for sure, so רב says she has no bond.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife who was definitely unfaithful
A wife who may or may not have been unfaithful

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; they belong to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: I am telling you about a definite sota,
and you are telling me about an uncertain sota!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא סוֹטָה וַדַּאי, וְאָמְרַתְּ לִי אַתְּ סוֹטָה סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: רב's rule applies only to a definite סוטה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule covers every סוטה, including an uncertain one
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means only a definite סוטה. An uncertain סוטה still needs חליצה.

steps.title: The Torah calls an uncertain סוטה 'defiled' too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes a definite סוטה different. If it is the Torah's word 'defilement', that word also appears about an uncertain סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about a definite סוטה? If it is because 'defilement' is written about her, then 'defilement' is written about an uncertain סוטה as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 2 by questioning the line between definite and uncertain. A proof is coming in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumed reason a definite סוטה loses her bond is that the Torah calls her טמאה. If the Torah uses טומאה for an uncertain סוטה too, the two cases should be treated the same, and step 2's answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Defilement; here, the Torah's word for a forbidden wife

phrases.english: And what is different about a definite sota
(what is the reason)
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves them out.

phrases.english: Is it because defilement is written about her?

phrases.aramaic: סוֹטָה סָפֵק נָמֵי טוּמְאָה כְּתִיבָא בַּהּ!
phrases.english: About an uncertain sota, defilement is written too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definite-versus-uncertain split made in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב means only a definite סוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason behind רב's rule (the word טומאה) applies equally to an uncertain סוטה.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי אלעזר on remarrying a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר: a man may not take back his divorcée if she was fully married to someone else, but he may if she was only betrothed, because the פסוק says 'after she was defiled'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי בן כיפר says in the name of רבי אלעזר: one who takes back his divorcée after she was married to another man, she is forbidden. After she was only betrothed, she is permitted, because it says, 'after she was defiled'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing the source that backs up its challenge. This first opinion sets up how the חכמים will read the same פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'defiled' as meaning she had relations with the second husband. Only full marriage (נישואין) involves that, so betrothal (אירוסין) alone does not forbid her to her first husband.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes back his divorced wife
Full marriage
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught:
Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar says
in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
One who takes back his divorced wife
phrases.notes: He means after she was with another man in between.

phrases.english: after full marriage, she is forbidden,
after betrothal, she is permitted,
because it is stated:
"after she was defiled."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the proof for the challenge in step 3
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah uses טומאה about an uncertain סוטה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן כיפר and the חכמים on 'אחרי אשר הוטמאה'

steps.title: The חכמים: 'after she was defiled' includes a סוטה who secluded herself
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים forbid the divorcée either way. They use 'after she was defiled' to include a סוטה שנסתרה, which shows that an uncertain סוטה is called 'defiled'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: both this one and that one are forbidden. Then how do I explain 'after she was defiled'? It comes to include a סוטה who secluded herself.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. The חכמים apply the word 'defiled' to a woman who only secluded herself, which is an uncertain case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who lawfully married someone else is not called 'defiled', so the חכמים move the פסוק to the סוטה. If a woman who only 'secluded herself' counts as 'defiled', then the Torah's טומאה covers an uncertain סוטה, which seems to prove the challenge in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this case and that case
How do I explain (this פסוק)?
To include
She secluded herself (with another man)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge rests on the phrase 'סוטה שנסתרה'. Secluding herself sounds like an uncertain case, and the חכמים still call her 'defiled'.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
both this one and that one, she is forbidden,
So how do I explain
"after she was defiled"?
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; it belongs to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: It comes to include a sota who secluded herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and makes the actual proof

steps.title: 'Secluded' is a polite word for actual relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'נסתרה' here means she actually had relations, and the ברייתא just used a polite word.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'secluded' mean? She had relations. And why does it call it 'secluded'? It used a polite expression.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof by saying the ברייתא is really talking about a definite סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'נסתרה' means she actually sinned, the ברייתא only calls a definite סוטה 'defiled'. That leaves the definite-versus-uncertain split from step 2 standing.

keyTerms.meaning: She had relations
A nicer, more polite way of saying something
He used (a word or phrase)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'נסתרה' literally here. The גמרא is saying the word is a polite way to describe real relations, not just being alone together.

phrases.english: And what is "secluded herself"? She had relations.
And why does it call it "secluded herself"?
It used a refined expression.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 5 by re-reading one key word
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא. The definite-versus-uncertain answer survives.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'נסתרה' means an uncertain case, but it can mean a woman who actually had relations.

steps.title: Why would she need a new source if her טומאה is already written?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the rejection. If she actually had relations, the Torah already calls her טמאה openly in the סוטה section, so why would the חכמים need 'after she was defiled'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If she had relations, then 'defilement' is already written openly about her: 'and she secluded herself, and she was defiled'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who definitely had relations is already called טמאה in the סוטה section itself. The חכמים would not need a different פסוק to include her, so their derivation must be about an uncertain סוטה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, explicitly
And she was defiled

steps.whyThisMatters: This puts the challenge from step 3 back on the table, so the definite-versus-uncertain defense of רב is under pressure again.

phrases.english: If she had relations, defilement is written explicitly about her:
"and she secluded herself, and she was defiled"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'נסתרה' means she actually had relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she definitely had relations, her טומאה is already written in the סוטה section, so including her through 'אחרי אשר הוטמאה' would add nothing.

steps.title: The extra words give a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים need 'after she was defiled' to add a לאו for a husband who stays with his סוטה wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: To place a prohibition (לאו) on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. The חכמים do not use the words to call her 'defiled'. They use them to add a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא asked: if נסתרה means she really had relations, the Torah already calls her טמאה, so why do the חכמים need 'after she was defiled'? The answer is that these words give a new law. A husband who lives with such a wife breaks a לאו. So the proof from step 5 stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: To establish upon her
A Torah prohibition (a 'do not' commandment)

phrases.english: To establish a prohibition upon her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 and so protects the rejection in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra phrase a different job: it adds a prohibition rather than a label.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase seemed extra if נסתרה means she really had relations, since the Torah already calls her טמאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase adds a לאו, so it is needed. It does not prove that an uncertain סוטה is called 'defiled'.

steps.title: No prohibition for a סוטה according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן כיפר holds there is no לאו for a סוטה, even when she definitely had relations with another man.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי בן כיפר does not hold that there is a לאו in the case of a סוטה, even if she definitely committed adultery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that רבי יוסי בן כיפר disagrees. For him there is no לאו here at all, even if the woman definitely had relations with another man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים used 'after she was defiled' for a לאו about a סוטה. רבי יוסי בן כיפר does not read the פסוק this way at all. So for him a husband who stays with his סוטה wife does not break this לאו, even in the definite case.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it
She committed adultery (definitely had relations)
Also

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar —
does not hold that there is a prohibition for a sota,
and the same applies even if she definitely committed adultery.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר לָאו בְּסוֹטָה לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving the חכמים' use of the phrase, the גמרא states רבי יוסי בן כיפר's opposite position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, there is no לאו against a husband staying with his סוטה wife, even when she definitely had relations with another man.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי בן כיפר reads the פסוק as being about marriage
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks of real betrothal and marriage, so it is about a divorcée who remarried and not about a סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? 'Becoming' and 'marriage' are written in this passage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוסי בן כיפר's view and answers right away. The passage speaks of a woman who truly became another man's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים say she 'becomes another man's' (הויה) and that the later husband 'took her as a wife' (אישות). These words describe a real, valid marriage. A סוטה cannot validly marry another man while she is still married, so the phrase 'after she was defiled' must be about a divorcée who remarried, not about a סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Becoming' another man's wife (betrothal)
Marriage

phrases.english: What is the reason?
'Becoming' and 'marriage' are written in it.
phrases.notes: דברים 24:2 ('and becomes another man's') and דברים 24:3 ('who took her as a wife').

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion stated in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why רבי יוסי בן כיפר sees no לאו in the case of a סוטה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The passage uses words of real marriage, so it speaks about a divorcée who remarried, not about a סוטה.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי בן כיפר, 'after she was defiled' is about a man taking back his divorcée who had married someone else. It is not about a סוטה, and he sees no לאו in a סוטה case.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks about the צרה of a taken-back divorcée
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks רב ששת: if a man took back his divorcée after she married someone else, and he died, what is the law for her צרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה asked רב ששת: a man took back his divorcée after she had married another man, and he died. What is the law for her צרה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב יהודה asks about the צרה (co-wife) of a woman whose husband took her back after she had married someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman herself is forbidden to her first husband, as the Torah teaches. The question is whether this prohibition also affects her צרה when the husband dies childless. In other words, is the צרה exempt from יבום like the צרות of the forbidden women in the משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him
One who takes back his divorcée
Her co-wife (her צרה)
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda asked Rav Sheshet:
One who took back his divorcée after she had married another man,
and he died, what is the law for her co-wife?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case of מחזיר גרושתו discussed in רבי יוסי בן כיפר's reading and opens a new question about the צרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the צרה of a remarried divorcée is exempt from יבום like the woman herself.

steps.title: No question according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר the answer is clear: the Torah's word 'defilement' is about this woman, so her צרה is like her.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, do not ask. He said that 'defilement' is written about one who takes back his divorcée, so her צרה is like her.
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא narrows the question. According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בן כיפר holds that 'after she was defiled' speaks about the taken-back divorcée. Earlier in the סוגיא, being called 'defiled' is what makes a woman's צרה share her status. So for him, her צרה has the same law as she does, and the question only remains open on another view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Do not ask it (there is no question)
Defilement (the Torah calls her 'defiled')
Like her (same law as her)

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar
do not ask it,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר
phrases.english: since Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar said
that 'defilement' is written about one who takes back his divorcée,
her co-wife is like her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב יהודה's question by showing it does not arise according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, the צרה of a taken-back divorcée has the same law as the woman herself, because the Torah calls this woman 'defiled'.

steps.title: Maybe 'היא' leaves out the צרה
steps.stepSummary: Someone might argue that 'תועבה היא' ('she is an abomination') limits the law to her alone, not her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say there is still a question because it is written about her 'she is an abomination'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible reason why the question could still exist for רבי יוסי בן כיפר. This sets up the next step, which rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'תועבה היא', 'SHE is an abomination'. The word 'היא' (she) could seem to limit the law to the woman alone. If so, her צרה would not share her status, even for רבי יוסי בן כיפר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is because of
'She is an abomination'

phrases.english: And if it is because it is written about her
phrases.notes: The idea is that 'היא' (she) might mean only her, and not her צרה. דברים 24:4.

phrases.english: 'she is an abomination,'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ תּוֹעֵבָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 12 that there is no question according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר the צרה is clearly like the woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'היא' in 'תועבה היא' seems to limit the law to the woman herself, which would leave out her צרה.

steps.title: 'היא' teaches about her children, not her צרה
steps.stepSummary: 'היא' teaches that she is an abomination but her children are not. So her צרה is still an abomination.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is an abomination, but her children are not abominations. This shows that her צרה is an abomination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The word 'היא' is already used to leave out her children, so it does not leave out her צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'היא' is already used for something else: only she is an abomination, but her children from this marriage are not. Since the word is used up on the children, it cannot also leave out the צרה. So her צרה has her status, and according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר there is no question.

keyTerms.meaning: But her children are not abominations
This shows that

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, the צרה of a man's taken-back divorcée is like her, because the Torah calls the woman 'defiled'. The word 'היא' only teaches that her children are not abominations, so it does not leave out the צרה.

phrases.english: She is an abomination,
but her children are not abominations;
phrases.notes: This is what 'היא' is used for, so it is not free to leave out the צרה.

phrases.english: so her co-wife is an abomination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and confirms step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the limiting word is already used for a different purpose.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'היא' limits the law to the woman alone, leaving out her צרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'היא' leaves out only her children. Her צרה is still an abomination, so according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר there is no question.

steps.title: Moving the question to the opinion of the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: Since the answer is clear according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, the גמרא asks the question according to the רבנן. They apply the word 'defilement' to a סוטה, but does the פסוק still keep its plain meaning about a man who takes back his divorcée?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, ask your question according to the רבנן. Even though they said the word 'defilement' is written about a סוטה, maybe a פסוק never fully loses its plain meaning. Or maybe once it has been pulled away from its simple meaning, it is pulled away completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא re-aims רב יהודה's question. It now asks it according to the רבנן, because according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר the answer was already clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use the word 'defilement' to teach about a סוטה. The doubt is whether the פסוק still says something about its plain subject, the man who takes back his divorcée. If it does, her צרה could be affected. If the פסוק was fully taken away from that subject, nothing is taught about this case at all.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of the Rabbis
A פסוק never loses its plain, simple meaning
Once it was uprooted, it is uprooted completely
A wife suspected of being unfaithful

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו' comes up all over ש"ס. Here the גמרא asks whether it still applies after the רבנן have used the פסוק for a different lesson.

phrases.english: When you ask it, ask it according to the Rabbis:
Even though the Rabbis said
that 'defilement' is written about a סוטה,
maybe a verse does not leave its plain meaning,
or perhaps, once it was uprooted, it is uprooted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 12-14 showed the answer is clear according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, so the question is moved to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the רבנן, does the פסוק still keep its plain meaning about a man who takes back his divorcée, so that her צרה is affected? Or was the פסוק fully uprooted to teach only about a סוטה?

steps.title: Second version: no question according to the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי) says there is no doubt according to the רבנן. Once the פסוק was taken away from its plain subject, it is fully taken away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: according to the רבנן, don't ask the question. Once the פסוק was uprooted, it is uprooted completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the discussion. In this version, the question does not start with the רבנן at all. This step sets up where the question really belongs, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, it is obvious for the רבנן that the פסוק no longer teaches anything about remarrying a divorcée. So for them there is no 'defilement' in this case, and her צרה is not affected. The doubt has to move somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of the discussion
Don't ask it: there is no question here

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first version the question is asked according to the רבנן. In the second version the רבנן are obvious and the question is asked according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: Some say: according to the Rabbis, don't ask it,
since once it was uprooted, it is uprooted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version that rejects asking the question according to the רבנן, choosing the side of 'כיון דאיעקר איעקר'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, the פסוק was fully uprooted from its plain subject, so there is no question.

steps.title: The question according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר: what does 'היא' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the question is asked according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר. He holds 'defilement' is about the man who takes back his divorcée. Does 'היא תועבה' leave out her צרה, or only her children?
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר: what is the law? He said 'defilement' is written about one who takes back his divorcée. Did the Torah limit it with 'she is an abomination', meaning her צרה is not? Or does it mean she is an abomination but her children are not, so her צרה is?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the second version, the גמרא asks the question according to רבי יוסי בן כיפר. The doubt is about what the word 'היא' ('she') is meant to leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, steps 13-14 treated it as obvious that 'היא' leaves out only her children. Here that same point becomes a real doubt. If 'היא' leaves out the צרה, she may do יבום. If it leaves out only the children, the צרה is forbidden like her.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who takes back his divorced wife
The Torah limited it: a word that leaves something out
Abomination
Co-wife: another wife of the same husband

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ — אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר, מַאי?
phrases.english: When you ask it, ask according to Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar: what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר
phrases.english: Even though Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar said
that 'defilement' is written about one who takes back his divorcée,
did the Merciful One limit it: 'she is an abomination',
phrases.notes: דברים 24:4. The word 'היא' ('she') is read as narrowing the law.

phrases.english: and her co-wife is not an abomination?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: הִיא תּוֹעֵבָה וְאֵין בָּנֶיהָ תּוֹעֲבִין,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: she is an abomination, but her children are not abominations,
but her co-wife is an abomination?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן כִּיפָּר מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the question according to the רבנן, the second version places the doubt with רבי יוסי בן כיפר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, does 'היא תועבה' leave out her צרה, or only her children, so that the צרה is still forbidden?

steps.title: רב ששת answers from a ברייתא about a fit and a disqualified widow
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells רב יהודה that the answer is found in a ברייתא. If one widow is fit and the other is disqualified, חליצה is done with the disqualified one, and יבום is done with the fit one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: you learned it in a ברייתא. If one woman was fit and the other disqualified: if he does חליצה, he does it with the disqualified one. If he does יבום, he does it with the fit one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רב יהודה's question by quoting a ברייתא. The case is two widows of a brother who died, one fit and one disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets the יבם choose: חליצה with the disqualified widow, or יבום with the fit one. רב ששת wants to read the 'disqualified' widow as a remarried divorcée, so that her צרה, the 'fit' one, may do יבום. Whether the ברייתא can be read that way is worked out in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it: points to a known ברייתא
Fit: a woman allowed to the יבם
Disqualified: a woman not fit for יבום
Performs חליצה, the ceremony that frees the widow without יבום
Performs יבום, marrying the brother's widow

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת tries to answer רב יהודה from a ברייתא: with a fit widow and a disqualified widow, חליצה goes to the disqualified one and יבום goes to the fit one. Steps 19-22 test this proof and then reject it.

phrases.english: He said to him: you learned it:
phrases.notes: רב ששת is answering רב יהודה's question from step 11.

phrases.english: If one was fit and one was disqualified,
if he would do חליצה, he does חליצה with the disqualified one,
and if he would do יבום, he does יבום with the fit one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question by pointing to a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא teaches that when one widow is fit and one is disqualified, חליצה is done with the disqualified one and יבום with the fit one. רב ששת means to read this as allowing יבום for the צרה of a remarried divorcée. This proof is rejected in steps 21-22.

steps.title: What do 'fit' and 'disqualified' mean in the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'fit' and 'disqualified' mean. It tests the first reading, 'fit or disqualified for everyone,' and finds a problem with it: for this יבם both women are allowed, so why would it matter which one he picks?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'fit' and what is 'disqualified'? If you say 'fit' means fit for everyone and 'disqualified' means disqualified for everyone, then since she is allowed to him, what difference does it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to analyze רב ששת's ברייתא. It is setting up a proof by first testing one way to read its words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on what kind of 'disqualified' the ברייתא means. If she is disqualified for people in general, for example from marrying a כהן, then she is still allowed to this יבם. Then there seems to be no reason for the ברייתא to tell him which woman to choose.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, allowed
Disqualified, not allowed
For everyone, in general
What difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: What is 'fit' and what is 'disqualified'?
If you say 'fit' means fit for everyone,
and 'disqualified' means disqualified for everyone,
since she is suitable for him,
what difference does it make to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the words of the ברייתא brought in step 18 so it can work as a proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'fit' and 'disqualified' mean fit or disqualified for everyone, or only for this יבם.

steps.title: The words must mean 'for him,' so the צרה of מחזיר גרושתו may do יבום
steps.stepSummary: So 'fit' and 'disqualified' must mean fit or disqualified for this man. That case is מחזיר גרושתו. The ברייתא allows יבום with the fit one, who is her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't 'fit' mean fit for him and 'disqualified' mean disqualified for him? And what case is that? One who took back his divorcée. And it teaches: if he wants to do יבום, he does יבום with the fit one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא chooses the second reading and uses it to answer the question from step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one kind of woman is forbidden to this man but allowed to everyone else: a woman his brother took back after divorcing her, when she had married someone else in between. Her צרה is the 'fit' one. The ברייתא lets him do יבום with the צרה, so 'היא תועבה' would leave out the צרה, not only the children.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that...? (starts a proof)
A man who takes back his divorced wife after she married someone else
And it teaches
Does יבום (marries his brother's widow)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that 'fit' means fit for him,
and 'disqualified' means disqualified for him,
and what is that case? One who took back his divorcée,
phrases.notes: His dead brother had taken her back, so she is forbidden to this יבם but allowed to other men.

phrases.english: and it teaches: and if he would do יבום,
he does יבום with the fit one!
phrases.notes: The 'fit' one is the צרה, the other wife, so the צרה is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first reading from step 19 and uses the second reading to prove the הלכה.
steps.raayaObject: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, 'היא תועבה' leaves out the צרה, so the צרה of מחזיר גרושתו may do יבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: חליצה with the disqualified one, יבום with the fit one.

steps.title: No, the words can still mean 'for everyone'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'Fit' and 'disqualified' really can mean fit or disqualified for everyone. The ברייתא still has a reason to choose between the women, because of רב יוסף's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, 'fit' means fit for everyone and 'disqualified' means disqualified for everyone. And what you asked, 'since she is suitable for him, what difference does it make to him?', the answer is because of רב יוסף's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes apart the proof by defending the first reading that step 19 had rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 rejected the 'for everyone' reading because it seemed to make no difference to the יבם. Now the גמרא says it does make a difference, for a reason that will be explained in the next step. If the 'for everyone' reading works, the ברייתא is not about מחזיר גרושתו, and there is no proof about the צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: No, really... (pushes back on a proof)
And what you said...
Because of רב יוסף's teaching

phrases.english: No, really 'fit' means fit for everyone,
and 'disqualified' means disqualified for everyone.
And what you said: since she is suitable for him,
what difference does it make to him?
It is because of רב יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 20 by bringing back the reading that step 19 had rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that the 'for everyone' reading made no difference to the יבם. It does make a difference, so the ברייתא need not be about מחזיר גרושתו.

steps.title: רב יוסף: do not waste what others may need
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that רבי taught a lesson here: a person should not pour out the water of his well when others need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף said: Here רבי taught: a person should not pour out the water of his well when others need it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב יוסף's teaching to explain why the choice still matters, even when both women are allowed to the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the choice makes no difference to him, it makes a difference to others. A woman who has done חליצה can no longer marry a כהן. So he should do חליצה with the woman who is already disqualified, and leave the fit woman able to marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Here רבי taught (a lesson hidden in the ruling)
A person should not pour out the water of his well
When others need it

steps.whatToRemember: The proof falls apart. 'Fit' and 'disqualified' can mean 'for everyone.' The ברייתא picks the disqualified woman for חליצה so the fit woman stays allowed to a כהן, just as you should not waste water that others could use.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling can have a hidden reason: avoiding needless loss to other people, even when the choice changes nothing for the person himself.

phrases.english: As רב יוסף said:
Here רבי taught:
a person should not pour out the water of his well,
when others need it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason that step 21 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should not waste something he does not need if others could use it. So חליצה is done with the woman who is already disqualified.

steps.title: A second ברייתא seems to show both women must do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: in the case of מחזיר גרושתו, 'she and her צרה do חליצה.' It fixes the wording to 'either she or her צרה,' which suggests the צרה cannot do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a man remarries his ex-wife after she was married to someone else, 'she and her rival wife do חליצה.' Can both of them really do חליצה? Rather, read it as 'either she or her rival wife does חליצה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to try to answer רב יהודה's question about the צרה. First it fixes the ברייתא's wording, because two widows can't both do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one widow ever does חליצה for a dead brother, so 'she and her צרה' can't mean both. Once it reads 'either she or her צרה,' the ברייתא gives חליצה as the only option for either woman. That would mean the צרה is also not allowed to do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
Rival wife: another wife of the same husband
She does חליצה, the release ceremony instead of יבום
Could it enter your mind? (something that can't be right)
Say / read it as

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who remarries his divorcée after she had married another man —
she and her rival wife perform halitza.
She and her rival wife — can that enter your mind?
phrases.notes: Only one widow does חליצה for the family, so both of them can't do it.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; it belongs to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: either she or her rival wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof from רבי's ברייתא was pushed off in steps 21-22, so the גמרא tries a different ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the צרה of a woman in the מחזיר גרושתו case is also not allowed to do יבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'המחזיר גרושתו משנשאת היא וצרתה חולצת,' read as 'either she or her צרה.'

steps.title: Since the wording is being fixed anyway, it can be fixed differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Since we already have to rework the ברייתא, we can rework it this way: she does חליצה, and her צרה may do either חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But aren't you already fixing the ברייתא's wording? Then fix it this way instead: she does חליצה, and her rival wife does either חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from step 23. The ברייתא's wording had to be changed anyway, so it can be changed in a way that allows the צרה to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on one particular way of fixing the text. Once the plain words can't be read as they stand, any reasonable fix will do. The new reading leaves רב יהודה's question still open.

keyTerms.meaning: You are already fixing up (the wording)
Fix it this way
She does יבום (marries the brother)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about מחזיר גרושתו proves nothing. Since its wording must be fixed anyway, it can be read to let the צרה do יבום.

phrases.english: But aren't you already fixing up its wording?!
Fix it this way instead:
She — performs halitza;
her rival wife — either performs halitza or enters levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes off the proof brought in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from this ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof depends on one fix of a text that must be fixed anyway. A different, equally good fix allows the צרה to do יבום.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks about the צרה in the case of a remarried divorcée
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that רבי יוחנן asked: in the case of מחזיר גרושתו, what is the law of her צרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן asked: if a man remarries his ex-wife after she was married to someone else, what is the law of her rival wife?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רבי יוחנן asks the same question רב יהודה asked: can the צרה of the remarried divorcée do יבום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the question was asked in ארץ ישראל too, not only by רב יהודה. The exact point of the question is sharpened in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question (a בעיא)
What is (the law)?
After she was married (to someone else)

phrases.english: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yohanan asked a question:
One who remarries his divorcée after she had been married to another man,
what is the law of her rival wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs for רב יהודה's question fail, the גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's version of the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the צרה of a woman in the מחזיר גרושתו case may do יבום.

steps.title: רבי אמי asks why not ask about the woman herself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי challenges: why ask only about the צרה? You should ask about the divorcée herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: then you should ask about her herself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי asks why the question skips the main woman. Her status should be the first thing in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a צרה's status follows from the main woman's status. So if her law is unclear, it seems odd to ask only about her צרה. רבי אמי pushes the asker to explain why she herself is not a question.

keyTerms.meaning: Then ask yourself / you should ask about
She herself

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
Then ask about her herself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the question in step 25 is framed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The framing of רבי יוחנן's question, which asks only about the צרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The main woman's status comes before her צרה's status. So if anything is unclear, it should be about her first.

steps.title: The woman herself is clearly forbidden by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The answer: there is no question about the woman herself. A קל וחומר forbids her. She became forbidden to her own husband, who was once permitted to her, so she is surely forbidden to the יבם, who was always forbidden to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: About her herself I have no question, because we say a קל וחומר: to the man who was permitted to her, she is forbidden. To the man who was forbidden to her, isn't it all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains that the divorcée herself is surely not allowed to do יבום, and gives the reason. The reason is a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her husband was once permitted to her, but after she married someone else, remarrying him became forbidden. The brother (the יבם) was always forbidden to her as his brother's wife. So if even the once-permitted man is now forbidden, the always-forbidden brother is surely forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
Permitted
Forbidden
All the more so

phrases.english: About her herself I have no question,
for we say a kal vachomer:
to the one who was permitted to her — she is forbidden;
phrases.notes: This is her husband: once permitted, now forbidden after she married someone else.

phrases.english: to the one who was forbidden to her — is it not all the more so?!
phrases.notes: This is the husband's brother, who was always forbidden to her as his brother's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's challenge from step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The divorcée herself is surely forbidden to the יבם through a קל וחומר, so there is no question about her.

steps.title: The real question: is a קל וחומר strong enough to exclude the צרה?
steps.stepSummary: The asker spells out the real question. Since the woman's prohibition comes from a קל וחומר, is that strong enough to also push off her צרה, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where I do have a question is: what is the law of her rival wife? Is a קל וחומר strong enough to push off a rival wife, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the question becomes sharp. The woman herself is forbidden, but is a prohibition that comes from a קל וחומר strong enough to also exclude her צרה from יבום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is no longer about the woman, whose status is settled. It is only about whether a rule learned through a קל וחומר has the power to affect her צרה too. The גמרא does not answer this. Instead it next brings a second version of the whole exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it strong (enough)?
To push off / exclude

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's question is narrow. The divorcée is surely forbidden through a קל וחומר. The open issue is whether that קל וחומר also excludes her צרה.

phrases.english: Where I do have a question:
her rival wife — what is the law?
Is a kal vachomer strong enough
to push off a rival wife, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the woman's own status in step 27, the asker restates the question about the צרה more precisely.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a prohibition learned through a קל וחומר is strong enough to also exclude the צרה from יבום.

steps.title: A second version of רבי יוחנן's question
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reports the exchange differently. רבי יוחנן's question is now asked about the woman herself, the מחזיר גרושתו case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק taught it this way: רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן asked: if a man takes back his divorcée after she was married to someone else, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts over with a different version of the same discussion. In this version, רבי יוחנן's question is about the remarried divorcée herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (steps 25-28), the woman was clearly forbidden and the question was about her צרה. Here רבי יוחנן leaves the צרה out entirely. He asks about the woman herself: may the brother do יבום with her if her husband dies?

keyTerms.meaning: Taught it this way. This introduces a different version of a discussion.
Asked, raised a question he could not resolve
One who takes back his divorced wife
After she was married (to another man)
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two versions! In the first version, the woman was obviously forbidden and the צרה was the question. In this version, it is the other way around.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak taught it this way:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said,
Rabbi Yochanan asked:
one who takes back his divorcée after she had been married, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the exchange from step 25 in a different version, in which the question is about the woman herself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a remarried divorcée may receive יבום from her late husband's brother.

steps.title: רבי אמי asks why the צרה is left out
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי asks why the question does not also include the woman's צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: And you should also be asking about her צרה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי pushes back. He asks why the question covers only the woman and not her צרה (her co-wife) as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when a woman cannot do יבום because she is an ערוה, her צרה is exempt too. So רבי אמי expects the question to cover the צרה as well. Leaving the צרה out seems to need an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Said to him
And you should ask (about this too)
Her צרה: the other wife of the same husband

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
And you should ask about her rival wife as well?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי: וְתִיבְּעֵי לָךְ צָרָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of the question in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of רבי יוחנן's question, which covers only the woman herself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the woman is in doubt, her צרה should be in doubt too, so the question should include both.

steps.title: The צרה is no question at all
steps.stepSummary: The reply is that the צרה is clearly not exempt, because a קל וחומר is too weak to push off a צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no question about her צרה, because a קל וחומר is not strong enough to push off a צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The reply (in this version, from רבי חייא בר אבא) explains that the צרה is obvious. She is not exempt, so there is nothing to ask about her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman's ban here comes only from a קל וחומר, not from an explicit פסוק. A ban that weak cannot reach out and also exempt the צרה. So whatever happens with the woman, the צרה stays bound to יבום or חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a question for me
Strong (enough)
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
To push off

phrases.english: Her rival wife is not a question for me,
because a kal vachomer is not strong enough
to push off a rival wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's challenge from step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר cannot exempt a צרה, so the צרה is obviously not exempt.

steps.title: The real question: can a קל וחומר override a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The real doubt is about the woman herself. Is a קל וחומר strong enough to forbid her even where there is a מצוה of יבום?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, my question is about the woman herself. What is the law? Is a קל וחומר strong enough to work even where there is a מצוה, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker now spells out exactly what he is unsure about. He wants to know whether the קל וחומר can forbid the woman herself to the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר seems to forbid her to the יבם. But יבום is a מצוה, and a ban that comes only from logic might not be strong enough to cancel a מצוה. That is the open question, the reverse of the first version, where the woman was obviously forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, where (my question is)
She herself
Where there is a מצוה (here, the מצוה of יבום)
Or not

steps.whatToRemember: In רב נחמן בר יצחק's version, the צרה is clearly not exempt. The open question is whether a קל וחומר can forbid the woman herself even against the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a general question about how strong a קל וחומר is: can a rule known only from logic push aside a מצוה from the תורה?

phrases.english: Rather, where I have a question,
it is about her herself, what is the law:
Is a kal vachomer strong enough
in a place of a מצוה, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי, הִיא גּוּפַהּ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After clearing away the צרה in step 31, this states the true question about the woman herself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a קל וחומר is strong enough to forbid the woman to the יבם even though יבום is a מצוה.
